Formula: CLI = 0.0588·L − 0.296·S − 15.8, where L = letters per 100 words and S = sentences per 100 words.

📖 How to use

  1. Paste your text into the box.
  2. Letters and sentences are counted per 100 words automatically.
  3. Read the Coleman-Liau Index: the US grade level needed to understand the text.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How is this different from Flesch-Kincaid?

Coleman-Liau uses characters instead of syllables: 0.0588×L − 0.296×S − 15.8, where L is letters per 100 words and S is sentences per 100 words.

What is a good Coleman-Liau score?

Scores map to US school grades: 8 means eighth grade. Aim under 10 for general audiences.

Why is it popular for automated checks?

Because it needs no syllable dictionary — letter counts are exact, so the score is deterministic and fast.
